transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah. I guess... well, I called EAP through work. It's just... lately, every little bang in the office is kind of getting to me. Like if someone shuts a file drawer too loud, or... drops a coffee mug. I just jump really hard. And then my chest just keeps racing way longer than it should. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried most days, even when there isn't a specific reason or trigger for it?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think so. It's mostly just... like I said, when there's a loud noise. If nothing's happening, I'm... I'm fine, I guess. I don't really just worry for no reason.
Do you ever feel anxious or on edge even when there’s no obvious reason or trigger around you?
Uh... I think you just asked me that. But... no. Like I said, it's really just the loud noises. I don't just sit around feeling on edge for no reason.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places or situations because you're worried about encountering loud noises?
Uh... no. I don't think so. I still go into the office and... do what I need to do. I haven't really stopped going anywhere.
When you jump and your chest races after a loud noise, do you find it hard to calm down afterward, like you stay keyed up or on high alert for a while?

Um... yeah, I guess so. Like... when I'm in the office now, I just kind of... keep checking where my boss is. Or where the exits are. Just seeing if anyone is coming up behind me. I'm supposed to be focusing on my team, but... I just keep looking around. So, yeah, I guess I stay a little keyed up.
Have you noticed yourself being more alert or watchful in situations where most people wouldn’t feel the need to be on guard, even when there aren’t any loud noises happening?
I mean... I just told you about the office. But other than that... no, not really. I don't think I'm just on guard everywhere I go.
Have you ever experienced or witnessed an event that involved actual or threatened serious harm, such as an accident, assault, or something else that was really frightening or traumatic?
Uh... no. Not really. I mean, I haven't been in any bad accidents or... anything like that. Just normal stuff, I guess.
Do you have a specific fear of loud noises that feels out of proportion to the actual danger they pose, even though you haven't experienced a traumatic event related to one?
No, I wouldn't say I'm afraid of them. I just... I don't like them. They just startle me, that's all. It's not a fear.
Have you noticed yourself feeling more irritable or easily annoyed lately, especially after being startled by a loud noise?
No, I don't think so. I mean... if something startles me, it's annoying for a second, but... I'm not snapping at people or anything. Just normal, I guess.

Have you experienced or been involved in any stressful or upsetting events recently, even if they weren't violent or life-threatening, that might be connected to why you're reacting this way to loud noises?
No... nothing like that. Work's been fine. Everything's just... normal. I really don't know why I'm jumping at things. I just am.
Have you ever noticed that you're more sensitive to sounds than other people, even before this started happening in the office?
No, I don't think so. I've always just been... average, I guess. Nothing bothered me before.
Have you noticed yourself being more reactive to other types of unexpected stimuli, like a sudden flash of light or someone touching you unexpectedly, even slightly?
Not really. Um... no. It's just the noises, I guess. I haven't noticed anything with lights or... people tapping me or whatever.
